A_target.statement:
Let $\CC$ be the [[Definition:Cantor Set|Cantor set]].
Then:
:$\map \lambda \CC = 0$
where $\lambda$ is [[Definition:Lebesgue Measure|Lebesgue measure]], and $\CC$ is [[Definition:Uncountable Set|uncountable]] with:
:$\card \CC = 2^{\aleph_0}$

B_source.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the set remaining at stage $n$ of the construction of the [[Definition:Cantor Set|Cantor set]].
Then $C_n$ is the [[Definition:Disjoint Union|disjoint union]] of $2^n$ [[Definition:Closed Real Interval|closed intervals]], each of length $3^{-n}$.

substitutions.the stage-n union of intervals: the nested sets whose intersection is C
substitutions.the finite total length (2/3)^n: an upper bound for the outer measure of C
substitutions.the branching count 2^n: the cardinality of the set of infinite binary addresses

validity_conditions: the stages must be nested and closed so continuity from above applies to Lebesgue measure
the first stage must have finite measure for continuity from above to be valid
the cardinality argument is independent of the measure argument and does not follow from it
proof_plan:
We have:
:$\displaystyle \CC = \bigcap_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty C_n$
where $C_0 \supseteq C_1 \supseteq C_2 \supseteq \cdots$

As $\map \lambda {C_0} = 1 < \infty$, by [[Measure is Continuous from Above]]:
:$\displaystyle \map \lambda \CC = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map \lambda {C_n}$

Each $x \in \CC$ has a unique [[Definition:Ternary Notation|ternary expansion]] $x = \displaystyle \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a_k} {3^k}$ with $a_k \in \set {0, 2}$.
The mapping $x \mapsto \sequence {a_k / 2}$ is a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] onto $\set {0, 1}^\N$.
Hence $\card \CC = 2^{\aleph_0}$.
{{qed}}
